issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry in the message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple of error message types includes 'transcriber_error' twice (once after 'auth_error/quota_exceeded_error/transcriber_error/input_error/commit_throttled' and again after that block). It's harmless functionally (tuple membership is idempotent) but is clearly a copy/paste mistake and should be removed for clarity.

issues.description: Error logging removed for the consolidated error branch
issues.detail: The previous code called logger.error(...) for 'error', 'auth_error', and 'quota_exceeded_error' before pushing the error frame. The unified branch now only calls push_error and drops the logger.error call. Even if push_error eventually surfaces something, the explicit log line was useful for ops — and the PR description explicitly says 'improve error handling to log all error types'. The new code logs none of them.

issues.description: Error type context is lost in push_error message
issues.detail: Previously each known error type produced a distinct prefix ('Error:', 'Auth error:', 'Quota exceeded:'). The new unified branch always emits 'Error: {error_msg}', so downstream consumers can no longer cheaply distinguish auth failures from quota exhaustion from generic errors. Consider including message_type in the pushed error string (e.g., f'{message_type}: {error_msg}').

issues.description: Behavior change on websocket disconnect not just a bug fix — silent failure mode
issues.detail: Removing the outer try/except around _process_messages does fix the infinite-loop-via-reconnect issue, but it also means any unexpected exception from the async-for loop now propagates out of _receive_messages instead of being warned about. The previous 'WebSocket connection closed: {e}' warning log is gone entirely. The reconnect machinery in websocket_service.py may handle this, but the loss of a diagnostic log line on disconnect should be intentional and noted; consider keeping a single logger.info/warning on exit from the async-for to preserve observability.

issues.description: Missing trailing newline in changelog file
issues.detail: changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline ('\ No newline at end of file'). Minor hygiene issue; most repo conventions expect a trailing newline.

issues.description: Per-message-type default error string is generic
issues.detail: data.get('error', f'Unknown error - {message_type}') is a reasonable fallback, but for types like 'auth_error' or 'quota_exceeded_error' the old defaults ('Authentication error', 'Quota exceeded') were more descriptive when the server omits an 'error' field. Minor regression in human-readability of fallback text.

issues.description: Inner try/except in _receive_messages still swallows all exceptions per message
issues.detail: The inner 'except Exception as e: logger.error(...)' inside the async-for catches any error from _process_response, which is broad. If _process_response raises due to a programming error, it will be logged at error level and the loop will continue silently. Worth considering whether some exception classes should propagate to trigger reconnect/teardown rather than being swallowed.

dissents.topic: Whether removing the outer try/except is the right fix vs. narrowing the caught exception

positions.position: Removing the outer try/except is the simplest correct fix — the reconnect loop in websocket_service.py is the right layer to handle disconnects, and catching here only re-masked the disconnect into a successful return that confused the outer loop. Ship it.

The correct fix would be to catch only the specific websocket-disconnect exception classes (e.g., ConnectionClosed, ConnectionClosedError) and re-raise everything else, while still emitting a structured log. Removing the try/except entirely loses the disconnect diagnostic and shifts policy to a distant module.

dissents.topic: Whether the unified error branch is an improvement

positions.position: Collapsing N near-identical elif branches into a single tuple membership check is a clear win — less code, easier to extend, and the previous per-type prefixes were marginally useful.

The old code preserved error category in both the log line and the pushed error string. The new code throws that signal away. The right refactor is a dict mapping message_type to (log_prefix, push_prefix) or simply f'{message_type}: {error_msg}', keeping the structural collapse while preserving categorization.

review.summary: The PR correctly addresses the two stated problems: it expands the list of recognized ElevenLabs error message types and removes an outer try/except that was masking websocket disconnects and causing an infinite reconnect loop. However, the consolidation regresses observability: the explicit logger.error calls for 'error'/'auth_error'/'quota_exceeded_error' were dropped, the disconnect warning log was dropped, the pushed error string no longer distinguishes error categories, and 'transcriber_error' is duplicated in the tuple. None are merge-blockers given the fix's importance, but the logging regression directly contradicts the PR description ('log all error types') and is worth a small follow-up before merge. The changelog file also lacks a trailing newline.
